lines.english: Sing, my tongue, the mystery of the glorious Body,

lines.latin: Sanguinísque pretiósi, quem in mundi prétium
lines.english: and of the precious Blood, which, as the price of the world,

lines.latin: fructus ventris generósi Rex effúdit géntium.
lines.english: the King of the nations, fruit of a noble womb, poured out.

lines.latin: Nobis datus, nobis natus ex intácta Vírgine,
lines.english: Given to us, born for us of a spotless Virgin,

lines.latin: et in mundo conversátus, sparso verbi sémine,
lines.english: and having dwelt in the world, the seed of the word once sown,

lines.latin: sui moras incolátus miro clausit órdine.
lines.english: He closed the days of His sojourn in a wondrous way.

lines.latin: In suprémæ nocte cœnæ recúmbens cum frátribus,
lines.english: On the night of the Last Supper, at table with His brethren,

lines.latin: observáta lege plene cibis in legálibus,
lines.english: the Law fully kept in the foods it prescribed,

lines.latin: cibum turbæ duodénæ se dat suis mánibus.
lines.english: He gives Himself as food to the Twelve with His own hands.

lines.latin: Verbum caro, panem verum verbo carnem éfficit:
lines.english: The Word made flesh, by a word, makes true bread His flesh:

lines.latin: fitque sanguis Christi merum, et si sensus déficit,
lines.english: and wine becomes the Blood of Christ; and if the senses fail,

lines.latin: ad firmándum cor sincérum sola fides súfficit.
lines.english: faith alone suffices to make a sincere heart firm.
So great a Sacrament, then, let us venerate with bowed heads:

lines.latin: et antíquum documéntum novo cedat rítui:
lines.english: and let the old law give way to the new rite:
let faith supply what the senses lack.
To the Begetter and the Begotten be praise and jubilation,

lines.latin: salus, honor, virtus quoque sit et benedíctio:
lines.english: salvation, honour, power also, and blessing:

lines.latin: procedénti ab utróque compar sit laudátio.
lines.english: to Him who proceeds from Both be equal praise.
